t.1.90.1: Janamejaya said: O brahmin, I have heard from you the great origin of my forefathers, and I have also heard of the noble kings in this lineage.
t.1.90.2: But this pleasing account, told so briefly, does not fully satisfy me; therefore let your honour tell it to me again, at greater length.
t.1.90.4: Their supreme glory, increased by the greatness of their true dharma and virtues, stands abundant, pervading the three worlds.
t.1.90.5: I am not sated as I listen to the story of those endowed with virtue, majesty, valor, vigor, strength and zeal, a story that is like the taste of the nectar of immortality.
t.1.90.3: This same divine tale, from Manu the Prajāpati onward, the holy origin of those kings: to whom would it not bring delight?
t.1.90.6: Listen, O king, to this entire auspicious account of the origin of your own lineage, which I once heard properly from Dvaipāyana as he recounted it.
t.1.90.7: From Dakṣa came Aditi; from Aditi, Vivasvān; from Vivasvān, Manu; from Manu, Ilā; from Ilā, Purūravas; from Purūravas, Āyus; from Āyus, Nahuṣa; and from Nahuṣa, Yayāti.
t.1.90.8: Yayāti had two wives: Devayānī, the daughter of Uśanas, and the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, Śarmiṣṭhā by name. Here there is a genealogical verse.
t.1.90.9: Devayānī gave birth to Yadu and Turvasu, and Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, bore Druhyu, Anu and Pūru.
t.1.90.10: Among them, from Yadu came the Yādavas, and from Pūru the Pauravas.
t.1.90.11: Pūru's wife was named Kausalyā. In her was born to him a son named Janamejaya, who performed three horse sacrifices and, having sacrificed with the Viśvajit, entered the forest.
t.1.90.12: Janamejaya married a Mādhavī named Anantā, and in her was born to him Prācinvant, who conquered the eastern quarter as far as the place where the sun rises; hence his name Prācinvant.
t.1.90.13: Prācinvān, indeed, married Aśmakī; in her was born to him Saṃyāti.
t.1.90.14: Saṃyāti, indeed, married the daughter of Dṛṣadvant, named Varāṅgī. In her was born to him Ahaṃpāti.
t.1.90.15: Ahaṃpāti, for his part, married the daughter of Kṛtavīrya, named Bhānumatī. In her was born to him Sārvabhauma.
t.1.90.16: Sārvabhauma, having conquered, carried off a Kaikeyī princess named Sunandā. In her was born to him Jayatsena.
t.1.90.17: Jayatsena married a princess of Vidarbha named Suṣuvā. In her was born to him Arācīna.
t.1.90.19: Mahābhauma married Suyajñā, the daughter of Prasenajit. To him, by her, was born Ayutanāyī, who brought about ten thousand human sacrifices; that is why he is called Ayutanāyī.
t.1.90.18: Arācīna, too, married another Vaidarbhī, named Maryādā. Of her was born to him Mahābhauma.
t.1.90.20: Ayutanāyī married the daughter of Pṛthuśravas, named Bhāsā. In her was born to him Akrodhana.
t.1.90.21: Akrodhana, indeed, married a Kāliṅga woman named Karaṇḍu. In her was born to him Devātithi.
t.1.90.22: Devātithi married a princess of Videha named Maryādā. In her, Ṛca was born to him.
t.1.90.23: Ṛca, indeed, married Sudevā, a daughter of the Aṅga king, and on her he begot a son, Ṛkṣa.
t.1.90.24: Ṛkṣa married the daughter of Takṣaka, named Jvālā. On her he begot a son named Matināra.
t.1.90.25: Matināra, indeed, performed a twelve-year sacrificial session on the Sarasvatī.
t.1.90.26: And when the sacrificial session had ended, Sarasvatī approached him and chose him as her husband. On her he begot a son named Taṃsu.
t.1.90.27: Here there is a genealogical verse.
t.1.90.28: Sarasvatī bore to Matināra a son, Taṃsu. Taṃsu begot a son, Ilina, in Kālindī.
t.1.90.30: Duḥṣanta married Viśvāmitra's daughter, named Śakuntalā. Of him, Bharata was born in her. Concerning this there are two ślokas.
t.1.90.29: Ilina, in turn, begot on Rathaṃtarī five sons, the first of whom was Duḥṣanta.
t.1.90.31: The mother is but a leather bag; the son belongs to the father, and he by whom he is begotten is that very one himself. Support your son, Duḥṣanta, and do not despise Śakuntalā.
t.1.90.32: O god among men, a son lifts up the one who sowed the seed from the abode of Yama. You are the one who placed this child in the womb; Śakuntalā has spoken the truth.
t.1.90.34: Bharata married Sunandā, the daughter of Sarvasena, a princess of Kāśī. To him and her was born Bhumanyu.
t.1.90.33: From that came his name, Bharata.
t.1.90.35: Bhumanyu married a Dāśārha woman named Jayā, and in her Suhotra was born to him.
t.1.90.36: Suhotra married a daughter of the Ikṣvākus named Suvarṇā, and by her was born to him Hastin, who had this city of Hāstinapura built; this is why it is called Hāstinapura.
t.1.90.37: Hastin married a Trigarta princess named Yaśodharā, and in her was born to him Vikuṇṭhana.
t.1.90.38: Vikuṇṭhana married a Dāśārha woman named Sudevā, and from her was born to him Ajamīḍha.
t.1.90.39: Ajamīḍha had one hundred and twenty-four sons, born of Kaikeyī, Nāgā, Gāndhārī, Vimalā and Ṛkṣā. They were kings, each the founder of a separate lineage. Among them, the one who carried on the dynasty was Saṃvaraṇa.
t.1.90.40: Saṃvaraṇa married Tapatī, the daughter of Vivasvat; in her was born to him Kuru.
t.1.90.41: Kuru married a Dāśārha maiden named Śubhāṅgī, and in her was born to him Viḍūratha.
t.1.90.42: Viḍūratha married a Magadhan woman named Saṃpriyā. In her was born to him a son named Arugvān.
t.1.90.43: Arugvān married a princess of Magadha named Amṛtā, and by her Parikṣit was born to him.
t.1.90.44: Parikṣit married a Bāhudā woman named Suyaśā, and by her Bhīmasena was born to him.
t.1.90.45: Bhīmasena married Sukumārī, a princess of Kekaya. In her was born to him Paryaśravas, whom they call Pratīpa.
t.1.90.46: Pratīpa married Sunandā, a princess of the Śibis, and on her he begot sons: Devāpi, Śaṃtanu, and Bāhlīka.
t.1.90.47: Devāpi, indeed, entered the forest while still a boy, but Śaṃtanu became the protector of the earth. On this there is a genealogical verse.
t.1.90.48: Whatever old man he touched with his two hands attained happiness and became young again; therefore they knew him as Śaṃtanu.
t.1.90.50: Śaṃtanu married Gaṅgā, the daughter of Bhagīratha. By her was born to him Devavrata, whom they call Bhīṣma.
t.1.90.49: That is why he bears the name Śaṃtanu.
t.1.90.52: In her was born to Parāśara, before her marriage, a son, Dvaipāyana. In her also two sons were born to Śaṃtanu, Citrāṅgada and Vicitravīrya.
t.1.90.51: Bhīṣma, wishing to do what would please his father, brought home Satyavatī to be his mother, she whom they call Gandhakālī.
t.1.90.53: Of those two, Citrāṅgada was slain by a Gandharva while he had not yet even reached youth, but Vicitravīrya became king.
t.1.90.54: Vicitravīrya married Ambikā and Ambālikā, the two daughters of the king of Kāśi, born of Kausalyā.
t.1.90.55: But Vicitravīrya, still without offspring, attained the bodiless state.
t.1.90.56: Then Satyavatī reflected, "The lineage of Duḥṣanta is being cut off."
t.1.90.57: She called to mind the seer Dvaipāyana.
t.1.90.59: She said to him: "Your brother Vicitravīrya has gone to heaven without any offspring; kindly beget offspring for him."
t.1.90.58: Standing before her, he said, "What shall I do?"
t.1.90.60: He said, "Very well," and begot three sons: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and Vidura.
t.1.90.61: There, through the granting of a boon by Dvaipāyana, a hundred sons were born to King Dhṛtarāṣṭra by Gāndhārī.
t.1.90.62: Of those sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, four were the foremost: Duryodhana, Duḥśāsana, Vikarṇa, and Citrasena.
t.1.90.63: Pāṇḍu had two wives, Kuntī and Mādrī, both of them jewels among women.
t.1.90.64: Then Pāṇḍu, while roaming on a hunt, saw a seer engaged in mating, coupling with a doe. As he was mounted in just that way, unsatisfied and not yet having tasted the pleasure of love, Pāṇḍu struck him with an arrow.
t.1.90.65: Pierced by the arrow, he said to Pāṇḍu: “Since I, while engaged in this act, have been struck down by you, who know the delight of love, before I could attain love's delight, therefore you too, on reaching this same state, will very quickly meet your death without attaining love's delight.”
t.1.90.66: Pāṇḍu, his face drained of colour, kept away from his two wives so as to avoid the curse.
t.1.90.68: "So you, for my sake, must bring forth sons," he said to Kuntī.
t.1.90.67: And he spoke these words: "Through my own rashness I have come to this; and I hear that there are no worlds for one who has no offspring."
t.1.90.69: There she bore sons: Yudhiṣṭhira by Dharma, Bhīmasena by Māruta, and Arjuna by Śakra.
t.1.90.70: Pāṇḍu, his face full of delight, said to her: “This co-wife of yours is childless; good lady, let offspring be produced in her as well.”
t.1.90.72: Then, in Mādrī, Nakula and Sahadeva were begotten by the two Aśvins.
t.1.90.71: He was told by Kuntī, “So be it.”
t.1.90.73: Indeed, seeing Mādrī adorned, Pāṇḍu conceived desire for her.
t.1.90.75: There, as he lay upon the funeral pyre, Mādrī ascended it after him.
t.1.90.77: Then the five Pāṇḍavas, together with Kuntī, were brought to Hāstinapura by the ascetics and presented to Bhīṣma and Vidura.
t.1.90.76: She said to Kuntī, "Noble lady, you must be vigilant in caring for the twins."
t.1.90.78: There too, in the house of lac, though they set about burning them, they were unable to do so because of Vidura's counsel.
t.1.90.79: And then, having slain Hiḍimba along the way, they went to Ekacakrā.
t.1.90.80: There in Ekacakrā, too, they slew the Rākṣasa named Baka and then went on to the city of the Pāñcālas.
t.1.90.82: And they begot sons: Yudhiṣṭhira begot Prativindhya, Vṛkodara Sutasoma, Arjuna Śrutakīrti, Nakula Śatānīka, and Sahadeva Śrutakarman.
t.1.90.81: From him they obtained Draupadī as their wife, and they returned safe and sound to their own land.
t.1.90.83: Yudhiṣṭhira, for his part, obtained at a self-choice ceremony the maiden named Devikā, daughter of Govāsana the Śaibya. On her he begot a son named Yaudheya.
t.1.90.84: Bhīmasena, too, married Baladharā, a princess of Kāśi, whose bride-price was valor; on her he begot a son named Sarvaga.
t.1.90.85: Arjuna, having gone to Dvāravatī, took as his wife Subhadrā, the sister of Vāsudeva. On her he begot a son named Abhimanyu.
t.1.90.86: Nakula, for his part, married Kareṇuvatī of Cedi as his wife, and on her he begot a son named Niramitra.
t.1.90.88: Bhīmasena, however, had earlier begotten on the Rākṣasī Hiḍimbā a son named Ghaṭotkaca.
t.1.90.87: Sahadeva, too, married at a svayaṃvara a Madra princess named Vijayā, and on her he begot a son named Suhotra.
t.1.90.89: These, then, are the eleven sons of the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.90.90: Abhimanyu married Virāṭa's daughter, Uttarā by name. In her a stillborn child was born to him.
t.1.90.92: And having revived him, he said: "Since he was born when the lineage had dwindled away, let this one be named Parikṣit."
t.1.90.91: Pṛthā received him on her lap at the command of Vāsudeva, the supreme person, who declared, “I shall bring this six-month fetus back to life.”
t.1.90.93: Parikṣit, for his part, married a woman named Mādravatī, and in her was born to him Janamejaya.
t.1.90.94: From Janamejaya, in Vapuṣṭamā, two sons were born: Śatānīka and Śaṅku.
t.1.90.95: Śatānīka, indeed, married a princess of Videha, and in her a son was born to him, Aśvamedhadatta.
t.1.90.96: Thus has this lineage of Pūru, and of the Pāṇḍavas, been recounted. Having heard this lineage of Pūru, one is released from all sins.
t.1.90.74: The moment he touched her, he became bodiless.
